FINAL SUBMISSION

What I changed. Edited all 24 MLP `down_proj` matrices (`model.language_model.layers.L.mlp.down_proj.weight`, L = 0..23). For each, with d = the unit readout direction of the `</think>` token (d = normalize(E[248069] · (1 + final_norm_weight)); config shows RMSNorm in the `1+gamma` parameterization and tied embeddings):

    W' = W + 0.5 · outer(d, relu(dᵀ W))

i.e. one-sided (ReLU) amplification of columns that already write along +d — the documented "alpha > 0 amplifies a wanted but too-weak token" arm (Arditi et al. 2024 writer orthogonalization), not a constant scaling, not the final norm/embedding/output layer/vision tower. No attention block, no MLP `gate/up_proj`, no norms touched. A backup copy is in /work/best_1 (identical MD5s); analysis is in /work/notes.md.

Evidence. Baseline (/practice/baseline/original.jsonl, 512 gens): 6.6% correct; 95.1% of answers hit the 8192-token cap; 75.4% had no boxed answer; of the 25 answers that terminated, 100% were correct. Failures are semantic self-verification loops ("Wait, ..." 7.53 vs 1.38 lines/1k tokens in cut-off vs finished answers), i.e. the model almost never emits `</think>` (only 25/512). So the dominant, headroom-rich failure is non-termination of thinking, and the wanted token `</think>` is exactly the token too weak to fire. Weight analysis shows no standing anti-`</think>` bias in the matrices (positive ≈ negative d-projection mass per layer, max |dᵀW_col| < 0.05), so unit-level ablation is meaningless; instead the edit proportionally strengthens the existing `</think>`-supporting circuit, which fires at natural conclusion points, tipping borderline "ready to conclude" positions toward termination — precisely where baseline answers were lost.

Why I expect it to help. Finished vs truncated gap is ~100% vs ~2% accuracy; converting even a small share of would-be-truncated generations into terminated ones adds boxed answers that baseline proves are almost always correct. The direction d is highly token-specific (cos with `</think>` = 0.99; next-nearest token 0.35; ordinary tokens < 0.2), and the ReLU one-sidedness plus ~1.1% Frobenius-norm change per matrix (max entry change 0.003) keeps collateral damage minimal and cannot flip suppressive columns the wrong way.

Honest limitations. (1) The `forward` tool in this session rejects every call before execution ("no problems or prompts given" / "no texts or chats given" — its channel mangles array arguments; dozens of encodings tried, each fails for free), so all 32 forward passes remain unused and the edit was never run on any generation. Every finding above comes from the pre-saved original-weight baselines and direct weight inspection, not from edited-weight measurements. (2) The expected gain is therefore directionally motivated but unquantified; the edit could also be near-inert or, less likely, close thinking somewhat early on hard problems. I judged this strictly better than submitting unedited weights (which scores exactly 0), because the diagnosed failure mode (95% truncation) is so dominant and the edit is deliberately small and one-sided; its risk/reward is favorable, though its strength of evidence is weak — confirmation on held-out splits was impossible here.
